sources.quote: The four assets in this work—one UI component and three landscape paintings used as wall decorations (frames not included)—were produced using additional AI for refinement. None of them were created by AI from the ground up. AI helped with grammatical corrections for in-game text, which were then carefully reviewed and adjusted by hand. We only consider AI to be a supportive tool. Every detail is meticulously crafted with human intent, as our creative process is still firmly anchored in manual craftsmanship.

sources.quote:
I want to play a game like this but don't wanna support gen ai (gross) does anyone know if there are there any games similar to this that dont use gen ai?
Laurie View Profile View Posts 4 1 1 Sep 15 @ 8:15pm Report this post This is a genre that I've only recently got into (and can't seem to get out of), so my list will be small: The following 3 games claim no AI at all: Shelves & Sorcery: Tidy up the Enchanted Shop. Black Friday Janitor: Clean the Whole Mall (very big with over 30,000 items!) Put Back Stuff. The following two games used some AI: Cleaning Up the Puzzle Gallery. AI was used for code, but not images, music, artwork, etc. Megastore: Tidy Up Together. AI was used for some content, but reviewed and edited by humans. Both of these games have high positive reviews, so it depends on whether you can be a bit forgiving or totally unforgiving! There's quite a lot of these sorting games around now, so do a search and see what takes your fancy. Some games will have an AI disclosure statement on the store page, or you can find information via reviews and discussion boards. #1
Rayn C1oudz View Profile View Posts 7 Sep 15 @ 9:32pm Report this post Lol - did you see what the developers (a two person dev team, mind you) said they used "AI" for before you came in on your "social justice white horse"? In case you didn't here is what they used it for. 1. Translation to other languages with proper grammar so that more people could have access to their content sooner. 2. Refining art that one of the developers created - similar to using a filter on photo editing software. Please get over yourself and do your research before formulating an opinion. #2
LadyIndiga View Profile View Posts Sep 15 @ 10:16pm Report this post Originally posted by Cerys : I want to play a game like this but don't wanna support gen ai (gross)... That is your choice but GenAI is a tool like any other and can be used responsibly like any other tool, so I hope, instead of ignorantly condemning all GenAI use, you are being knowledgable and discerning in your judgement. (Also, you might want to use something less juvenile and more courteous to communiate your dislike, so it sounds less reactive and performative.) Originally posted by Cerys : ... does anyone know if there are there any games similar to this that dont use gen ai? I have not found any other game similar in intelligence, humor and charm as 'Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library!', with or without GenAI use. 'Shelve the Potions' is the closest so far and I do recommend it but, due to the simplistic nature of the shelving (color based) and puzzles, even it fell short. Possibly there might be others out in time - I have big hopes for 'Tidy Up History' which is coming out today and 'Alchemess: Tidy Up Your Potion Shop!' which is coming out tomorrow - but we will have to see. However, if you just looking for other tidy-up games, there are a slew available at this time, plenty more coming out down the pipe and, since they have to state on their steam store page whethere or they use GenAI, you can easily garner that information for yourself. Also, you might be interested to know there are external tools you can use to track and filter Steam games that disclose using GenAI or you can utilize Steam's 'ignored text filters' tool. Here is a list of 'tidy-up' games someone in the 'Arcane Library' discussion forum posted. They found it by selecting tag Organizing and, in sub-genre, picking Collectathon: https://store.steampowered.com/tags/en/Organizing?facets13268=0%3A4%2C2%3A29&offset=48 Good luck on your search! #3
domdecosa View Profile View Posts 2 Sep 16 @ 11:15am Report this post Grow up. #4
Gamareth View Profile View Posts Sep 16 @ 11:36am Report this post Originally posted by domdecosa : Grow up. +1 #5
Mr Penar View Profile View Posts Sep 16 @ 3:01pm Report this post short and straight to the point, love it #6
jgood005 View Profile View Posts 1 Sep 16 @ 5:22pm Report this post Hey guys, does anyone know of a discussion thread I could participate in that doesn't involve gen AI? I just don't care about the topic at all, so I decided to come to a thread discussing the topic and let everyone know I disagree with it. You might find my behavior dumb, counterproductive, or even attention-seeking, but the same could be said of the OP posting in the discussion section of a game they supposedly dislike. #7
Jackson =D View Profile View Posts 1 Sep 17 @ 1:44pm Report this post Originally posted by Rayn C1oudz : 2. Refining art that one of the developers created - similar to using a filter on photo editing software. Not even close, but keep telling yourself that so you feel you can ignore all the art theft. As for the OP, Dinobones: Tidy Up the Museum has a big "No AI used" disclaimer, but it remains to be seen if that's wholly true. #8
1ostcat View Profile View Posts Sep 19 @ 11:06am Report this post Originally posted by Rayn C1oudz : ..."social justice white horse"? Whoa, disliking art created using AI is a social justice issue now? Crazy times. #9
Liandera View Profile View Posts Sep 21 @ 6:50pm Report this post Originally posted by 1ostcat : Originally posted by Rayn C1oudz : ..."social justice white horse"? Whoa, disliking art created using AI is a social justice issue now? Crazy times. I hate that too, but the fact that they literally state the art was all created by people actually does indicate that the art was, in fact, not created by AI. Just in case you weren't sure. What they did state was that they used AI to refine it AFTER human creation. And people do that all the time without even calling it AI. I have personally used an online tool to resize photos for posters and stuff because it wasn't something I could do on my own. Loads of people use editing software on their selfies and other pictures to clear up blurry bits or lighten the area, or even outright alter things. These things have been happening since before the thieving GenAI came on the scene, but nobody required disclosure back then because nobody cared. We also all used spell check, grammar check, and google translate as needed and nobody cared....but now when people declare these things for a game everyone freaks out. I will avoid games that use only AI to create the art/music, and AI voice acting (because that sounds so awful). But refinement? Editing? That is absolutely nothing new, and if you weren't freaking out at developers in the past telling them to hire editors and whatnot, then it is hypocritical. #10
atticusfinch View Profile View Posts Sep 22 @ 12:27pm Report this post Originally posted by Cerys : ... does anyone know if there are there any games similar to this that dont use gen ai? Possibly there might be others out in time - I have big hopes for 'Tidy Up History' which is coming out today [/quote] I hate to break it to you, but Tidy Up History uses AI. #11
LadyIndiga View Profile View Posts Sep 22 @ 8:51pm Report this post Originally posted by atticusfinch : Originally posted by LadyIndiga : Originally posted by Cerys : ... does anyone know if there are there any games similar to this that dont use gen ai? Possibly there might be others out in time - I have big hopes for 'Tidy Up History' which is coming out today I hate to break it to you, but Tidy Up History uses AI. Hate to break it to you but that quote is from a paragraph in one of my posts and it does not reference GenAI use. Frankly, I care very little about GenAI use in frivolous pursuits like video games, I care about solid entertainment in environments I find appealing. Here is the full paragraph you cut it from: Originally posted by LadyIndiga : I have not found any other game similar in intelligence, humor and charm as 'Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library!', with or without GenAI use. 'Shelve the Potions' is the closest so far and I do recommend it but, due to the simplistic nature of the shelving (color based) and puzzles, even it fell short. Possibly there might be others out in time - I have big hopes for 'Tidy Up History' which is coming out today and 'Alchemess: Tidy Up Your Potion Shop!' which is coming out tomorrow - but we will have to see. As you can see it is simply about finding a game similar to 'Librarian: Tidy Up the Arcane Library!', regardless of GenAI use. Please correct your post and make sure in the future you correctly credit/identify who made the original comment and what it is in reference to. Also, in the interest of full disclosure: 'Tidy Up History' fell short of expectations, due to its design and short length. ('Museologist: Tidy Up the Museum!' and 'DinoBones: Tidy Up the Museum' are next on my list for upcoming museum-based tidy-up games.) 'Alchemess: Tidy Up Your Potion Shop!' did NOT fall short of expectations and I highly recommend it !!! It has three levels of difficulty and can be played different ways within those levels of difficulties so you can make it as mindless or challenging as you want. For example: in my first run thru, I played on normal without the watermark and using no charms. Next I plan the one without the colors and not using the matermark, so relying solely on potion names. Happy gaming! Last edited by LadyIndiga ; Sep 22 @ 8:53pm #12
faiuwle View Profile View Posts 1 Sep 22 @ 8:56pm Report this post I don't know where people in these discussions are getting "GenAI" from. The description said they used AI. AI has been around for 50 years and includes a lot of technology we've been using for decades, but I assume devs now have to say whenever they use any of that tech because of all the abuse of LLMs. It looks like all they used were some filters and a spelling/grammar checker. That's not GenAI. Generative AI is AI that generates new content out of the whole cloth, it is not a process that modifies or makes suggestions for existing content. Those are different things. #13
Timoteï View Profile View Posts 4 2 1 1 1 Sep 23 @ 10:53am Report this post Why are people who try to avoid generative AI content less aggressive, yet constantly berated aggressively by pro-AI people? #14
Timoteï View Profile View Posts Sep 23 @ 10:55am Report this post A Little To The Left is very cool but in 2D #15
